summary: Inbound requests converge on a protected site at the centre of a dotted globe. Blocked ones dent its shield ring and burst off it.

props.name: target
props.description: `{ label, lat, lon }` of the protected site. The globe faces it, so it sits at the centre of the disc; the label shows in the header and the accessible summary.

props.name: events
props.description: Requests: `{ id, lat, lon, verdict, region?, time? }` with `verdict` `blocked` or `allowed`. Each new `id` animates once, so the array can grow or be replaced. Without it a seeded demo stream runs; an empty array shows an empty window that `push()` can fill.

props.name: maxInFlight
props.description: Arcs drawn at once. Further requests go straight into the counts.

props.name: windowSeconds
props.description: Window for the counts, the origin list and the rate chart, in seconds, 1 to 3,600. Requests older than the window are ignored.

props.name: shieldRadius
props.description: Radius of the shield ring in px, 10 to 120 and at most 60 % of the globe's radius.

props.name: live
props.description: Runs the demo stream while `events` is not given. Off keeps the prefilled demo window as it is, until a request is pushed.

props.name: onEvent
props.description: Called when a request reaches the shield (blocked) or the site (allowed). Requests without an arc call it as soon as they are counted.

methods.description: Adds one request, with or without `events`. An id that was already seen is ignored.

accessibility: The globe stage has `role="img"` and an `aria-label` that summarises the window, for example "Requests to eu-central. In the last minute: 1,284 blocked, 312 allowed, most from ap-south." It is refreshed at most every 15 seconds.

The counters, the site label, the origin list and the peak rate are real text. Each origin row has a visually hidden sentence with its region, total, blocked and allowed counts; the rolling digits and the dotted bars are `aria-hidden`.
Both globe canvases, the rate chart canvas, the server placeholder and the target square are `aria-hidden`. The globe takes no pointer or keyboard input.
motion: With reduced motion no arcs, dents or sparks play: each request lights the shield dots facing its origin for 400 ms and is counted at once, the counts swap without rolling and the origin rows change places without sliding.
notes: The globe always faces the target and never turns, so each arc is projected once. Arcs rise higher the farther they travel; origins on the far side climb over the horizon, where a two-dot glint marks the arc.

Packets speed up toward the site and take 1 s plus up to 0.8 s for the far side of the world. A blocked packet stops at the ring: the dots around the impact dent inward on springs, heat up and throw ten sparks off the ring like a reflection. An allowed packet parts the ring, passes and lands with a small ring of lit dots around the site.

Requests are grouped by `region`. Without it, a request counts toward the nearest of 16 generic regions (`us-east`, `us-west`, `sa-east`, `eu-west`, `eu-central`, `eu-north`, `me-central`, `af-south`, `ap-south`, `ap-southeast`, `ap-northeast`, `au-east`, `us-central`, `ca-central`, `eu-south`, `ap-east`) by great-circle distance.

Counts cover the last `windowSeconds`, by each request's `time` (or when it arrived). The origin list shows the five regions with the most requests and re-sorts at most once a second; each row has a dotted bar with the region's share of all requests, blocked dots first. From 560 px of width a dotted chart of requests per second with the peak sits under the list, so a flood shows as a spike.

Requests older than 10 seconds, requests that arrive while the globe is off screen or the tab is hidden, and requests beyond `maxInFlight` are counted without an arc. Ids are remembered (the last 4,000), so a re-render with the same array never counts them twice. A new `target` counts the arcs in flight at once and redraws the globe.

The stage is square, at most 420 px wide; from 560 px of container width the origin list stands beside it, else below. Arcs draw on a canvas that reaches 40 px above and below the stage and 16 px to the sides (40 px from 500 px of width).

The server markup shows the disc with a 30° graticule, the shield ring and the target; it fades to the dotted globe after the first frame. The animation loop pauses while the globe is off screen and stops when nothing moves.
Switching between demo data and `events` starts the panel over, so demo counts never mix with your requests.

data.note: Pass your requests as `events`, or call `push()` on the ref for a live feed; an empty array shows "No requests in the last minute". Without `events` the component shows a seeded demo stream of about four requests a second, 80 % blocked, from invented sources around real cities, on a prefilled window of invented counts.
